chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) would, when it was the night of the twenty-first and the twenty-third, begin supplicating until the night passed; and when the night passed, he would pray.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir do on the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Khisal* highlights the devotional intensity of Imam al-Baqir (AS) during the odd nights of Ramadan, specifically emphasizing the transition from prolonged *du'a* to *salat* after midnight. In Shia tradition, these nights are central to the search for Imam Ali’s martyrdom and the culmination of Ramadan’s blessings, making this practice a model for *Ihya al-Layl* (awakening the night) and spiritual preparation for Eid al-Fitr.
